rv.q: Director Tatyana-Marie Carlo does a great job handling the drastically shifting tones and rhythms of the piece as the four main actors believably display the growing bonds of their characters.
They’re absolutely awful to each other and they’re also, in their misfiring attempts to build themselves into grown-up children, utterly lovable.

cn.t: Jesús I. Valles's high school drama earns praise for its authentic portrayal of teenage boys navigating friendship and identity, with critics highlighting the sharp dialogue and compelling performances that bring the ninth-grade characters to life.
